rv.q: Here is the play of this year and last year and quite possibly next year as well.
Daldry’s production is particularly strong on hauntings, creating tear-pricking moments that fill the stage with a cavernous sense of loss.
Trust me, you don't want to be that person at the dinner table a decade from now, wishing you'd got tickets to The Inheritance while everybody else at the party still raves about it.

Equally satisfying as comedy, drama and debate, highlights for me included a party scene in which liberals discover they’ve a republican in their midst and a hilarious set piece wedding with the gasp-out-loud HOWARD'S END revelation still packing a punch.
Two parts, three hours fifteen minutes each – it's a big ask, but it's a rewarding one.

cn.t: Matthew Lopez's epic seven-hour exploration of gay life in New York earns acclaim for its flowing, intimate storytelling and gentle wit, with critics hailing it as era-defining despite its daunting length.
